problem:
A total of $2$ milliliters of water evaporate from a beaker every second.
What differential equation describes the rate of change of the amount of water $W$ (in milliliters) remaining in the beaker?  Assume that the time $t$ is measured in seconds.
worked_solution:
If the amount of water in the beaker is $W$ milliliters, then the rate of change of the amount of water is $\frac{\text{d}W}{\text{d}t},$ where $t$ is the time in seconds.

Since $2$ milliliters of water are lost every second, the rate of change of the amount of water is given by the differential equation

$$
\frac{\text{d}W}{\text{d}t}=-2.
$$

The right-hand side is negative because the beaker is losing water.
